questions.questionText: Which supply curve shows that the price elasticity of supply of the good is always equal to 1?

options.A: a straight line that intersects the horizontal axis
options.B: a straight line that intersects the vertical axis
options.C: a straight line that passes through the origin
options.D: a straight line that is vertical to the horizontal axis

questions.questionText: What is a distinguishing feature of a progressive income tax?

options.A: High earners pay a higher proportion of their income in tax than low earners.
options.B: High earners pay a lower proportion of their income in tax than low earners.
options.C: High earners pay the same proportion of their income in tax as low earners.
options.D: Low earners pay more tax than high earners.

questions.questionText: Why might a government nationalise a private firm?

options.A: to gain greater efficiency due to more competition
options.B: to increase merit good provision
options.C: to increase choice for the consumer
options.D: to raise more tax revenue

options.A: high high
options.B: high low
options.C: low high

questions.questionText: Compared with Pakistan, Germany has a higher output of pharmaceuticals per unit of resources used. What could explain this?

options.A: the existence of floating exchange rates
options.B: the law of absolute advantage
options.C: the Marshall–Lerner condition
options.D: the terms of trade

questions.questionText: Which statement about inflation is correct?

options.A: Inflation will lead to a rise in exports.
options.B: Inflation will lead to a rise in real incomes.
options.C: Inflation will lead to a rise in the cost of living.
options.D: Inflation will lead to a rise in the purchasing power of money.

questions.questionText: Why is it that a country’s balance of payments must always balance?

options.A: Exchange rate changes will correct any deficit or surplus.
options.B: One country’s deficit is balanced by another country’s surplus.
options.C: The current account is balanced by the capital and financial accounts.
options.D: The government must act to correct any disequilibrium.

questions.questionText: Which argument for protection would be most relevant if the government of country X decided to exercise voluntary export restraint in its trade with country Y?

options.A: Voluntary export restraint would achieve an immediate correction for X’s balance of trade deficit.
options.B: Voluntary export restraint would cause the level of GDP to increase in country X.
options.C: Voluntary export restraint would help to negotiate improved trading conditions between X and Y.
options.D: Voluntary export restraint would help to reduce the level of unemployment in country X.

questions.questionText: The average price of a country’s exports increased by 5% and the average price of its imports increased by 10%. What can definitely be concluded from this information?

options.A: Its balance of trade will improve.
options.B: Its balance of trade will worsen.
options.C: Its terms of trade have improved.
options.D: Its terms of trade have worsened.

questions.questionText: There is an increase in indirect taxes. What will be the impact on demand-pull inflation and on cost-push inflation? demand-pull cost-push inflation inflation

options.A: fall fall
options.B: fall rise
options.C: rise fall
options.D: rise rise

options.A: Laura

questions.questionText: Which condition is necessary for a country’s balance of payments on its current account to improve if it reduced its exchange rate?

options.A: Both the price elasticities of supply for its imports and its exports must be elastic.
options.B: The importing country will buy all the excess supplies of its trading partner to clear the market.
options.C: The sum of the price elasticities of domestic demand for imports and the foreign demand for exports must be greater than one.
options.D: The trading partners need to agree on the maximum prices to be charged for imports and exports.

questions.questionText: What would make a policy of raising interest rates less likely to be effective in reducing inflation?

options.A: Aggregate supply is increasing faster than aggregate demand.
options.B: Consumers expect prices to rise even faster in the future.
options.C: Consumers’ spending is largely paid for on credit.
options.D: Interest rates are still higher abroad.
